```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```

`tidytmle` brings cross-fitted Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (CV-TMLE) into the `tidymodels` ecosystem around a clear 4-step human workflow: **Question $\rightarrow$ Estimate $\rightarrow$ Audit $\rightarrow$ Paper**.

If you want to understand *why* this two-step estimator outperforms regression alone or weighting alone, start with [TMLE Intuition: A Step-by-Step Visual Guide](tmle-intuition.html).

## Step 1 · Ask Your Question & Fit Safe Defaults

Declare which column is the `outcome`, which is the `treatment`, and which covariates (`W`) you want to adjust for using `tidyselect`, then call `fit()`. Cross-validated Super Learning, adaptive overlap bounds, and bounded logistic calibration turn on automatically:

```{r level1, message = FALSE}
library(tidytmle)

cohort <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 350, outcome_type = "binary", seed = 42)

fit <- tmle_spec(
  outcome    = y,
  treatment  = a,
  covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),
  estimand   = c("ate", "rr", "or")
) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 5L) |>
  fit(data = cohort)

fit
```

Visualize the causal conclusions right away with `autoplot(fit)` (defaults to the forest contrast plot `type = "effect"`):

```{r effect-plot, fig.alt = "Causal effect forest plot showing targeted ATE, Risk Ratio, and Odds Ratio with 95% confidence intervals"}
autoplot(fit)
```

## Step 2 · Read Plain-English Findings & Tidy Tables

Every `tidymodels` extraction verb works out of the box—plus plain-English summaries, simultaneous confidence bands, and sensitivity E-values:

```{r verbs}
# Plain-English causal interpretation
summary(fit)

# Publication numbers with simultaneous bands & VanderWeele-Ding E-values
tidy(fit, simultaneous = TRUE, e_value = TRUE)

# Cross-validated nuisance performance & Super Learner ensemble weights
collect_metrics(fit)
extract_sl_weights(fit)
```

## Step 3 · Audit Causal Health & Stress-Test Instantly

Run `check_tmle(fit)` to evaluate the 5 pillars of causal trustworthiness (*Targeting Convergence*, *Comparison Overlap*, *Confounder Balance*, *Individual Influence*, and *Model Learning Quality*), inspect the 4-panel dashboard, and test stricter assumptions in milliseconds via `retarget()`:

```{r audit, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 6.8, fig.alt = "4-panel Tufte-styled TMLE Causal Audit Dashboard showing overlap, targeting shift, sensitivity sweep, and confounder balance dumbbell plot"}
check_tmle(fit)

if (requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
  autoplot(fit, type = "dashboard", g_grid = seq(0.01, 0.12, by = 0.02))
} else {
  autoplot(fit, type = "overlap")
}

# Instant sensitivity check without ML refitting
fit_strict <- retarget(fit, g_bounds = c(0.05, 0.95))
fit_att    <- retarget(fit, estimand = "att")
fit_older  <- retarget(fit, subgroup = age >= 55)

dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit), scenario = "Adaptive bounds (All)"),
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_strict), scenario = "Strict bounds [5%, 95%]"),
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_att), scenario = "Among treated (ATT)"),
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_older), scenario = "Subgroup age >= 55")
) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, estimand, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)
```

## Step 4 · Generate Paper- & Blog-Ready Prose

Use `report_tmle()` to draft complete **Methods**, **Results**, and **Causal Assumptions** paragraphs automatically populated from the exact models, bounds, and diagnostics in your fit (`style = "paper"`, `"plain"`, or `"markdown"`):

```{r report}
report_tmle(
  fit,
  outcome_label = "clinical recovery",
  treatment_label = "targeted therapy",
  style = "paper"
)
```
